rules.title: Make overview pages answer reader questions
rules.rule: About and overview pages should answer a reader's actual questions, not narrate the navigation. Skip repeated brand-name heroes, vague mission/tagline filler, and tours of every section; keep concrete identity, ownership, contact, and policy facts where they help the reader.
rules.example: About / Employee-owned design studio. / Contact hello@example.org.
rules.counterexample: Studio / About / A creative home for meaningful experiences. / Browse the projects and learn about the team.
rules.rationale: An overview should provide concrete identity and useful facts.

rules.title: Let the argument set the length
rules.rule: Let the argument determine paragraph length and structure. Do not arbitrarily limit or extend length of text to fit a predefined amount.
rules.example: Use two sentences for a simple result and a longer paragraph for its limitations.
rules.counterexample: Expand every result to exactly five sentences.
rules.rationale: Arbitrary length targets can distort the explanation.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/fac/_template/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Keep details that matter to the audience
rules.rule:
**DO NOT say things that do not matter to the audience.**

Keep a detail only when it helps the reader understand the subject, make a decision, or take the intended action. A fact being true or available is not a reason to include it. Cut internal bookkeeping, process narration, unrelated history, and implementation details unless the audience needs them. Keep qualifications that materially affect the reader's decision; state them once, plainly.
rules.example: The letter gives the applicant’s relevant experience and the requested next step.
rules.counterexample: The letter narrates internal draft filenames and revision counters.
rules.rationale: Readers need details that support understanding, decisions, or action.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing SKILL.md guidance. Examples are illustrative; see deslopify/examples/website-copy.md.

rules.title: Delete repetition
rules.rule: Delete repetition that adds no information. Nothing in a single slide should be filler for things that have already been said, especially titles and visual metadata.
rules.example: The result appears once, where the argument needs it.
rules.counterexample: Repeat the result in the slide title, subtitle, chart label, and closing sentence.
rules.rationale: Repetition uses attention without adding information.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/fac/_template/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Do not use polish as proof of authorship
rules.rule: Do not treat punctuation or polish as proof that writing is AI-generated. AI-generated language usually uses specific words or phrases.
rules.example: Assess what a sentence says and whether its wording fits the context.
rules.counterexample: Declare a passage AI-generated solely because it uses an em dash.
rules.rationale: Punctuation and polish alone do not establish authorship.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Do not manufacture human errors
rules.rule: Do not add typos, tangents or invented details to imitate a human.
rules.example: Preserve the supported result and the writer’s actual qualification.
rules.counterexample: Add a deliberate typo and an invented personal story to sound human.
rules.rationale: Fabricated mistakes and details damage meaning and accuracy.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Avoid automatic aphorism endings
rules.rule: Do not end every paragraph by restating its point as an aphorism.
rules.example: End the paragraph after the result and its needed limitation.
rules.counterexample: Append “Ultimately, progress is the art of possibility” after every paragraph.
rules.rationale: A repeated closing flourish adds little information.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Choose words for their meaning
rules.rule: Choose wording for meaning, not for a stock phrase checklist.
rules.example: Keep “robust” when it describes resistance to outliers and the analysis supports it.
rules.counterexample: Remove “robust” solely because it appears on a list of AI words.
rules.rationale: A phrase list does not determine whether wording serves the reader.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/fac/_template/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Omit unneeded version history
rules.rule: Omit history about old versions, retired pages, migrations, or redesigns when users can use the current experience without it, especially in prominent notices. Prefer the current action or a transparent redirect. Keep migration notices needed for user action, data loss, compatibility, or service impact.
rules.example: Current navigation works, so omit the old-pages notice. Keep “Export your data by June 30 to avoid losing access” when action is required.
rules.counterexample: The older pages of this site now live on the home page. Start there.
rules.rationale: Keep notices when they communicate an actual consequence or required action.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing SKILL.md guidance. Examples are illustrative; see deslopify/examples/website-copy.md.

rules.title: Preserve the author’s voice
rules.rule: Keep the author’s voice while making the requested edits.
rules.example: Keep “I built this to make mornings easier” while correcting an unclear reference.
rules.counterexample: Replace it with “We are delighted to empower productive daily workflows.”
rules.rationale: Editing should preserve the writer’s intended voice.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/fac/_template/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Preserve useful and accessible UI copy
rules.rule: Keep copy that supplies needed context or navigation, accessible names and alt text, instructions, errors, product facts, and legal disclosures. A useful heading or label earns its place; minimalism is not a reason to remove it.
rules.example: Keep “Choose a size before adding to cart,” the accessible button name, and the returns disclosure.
rules.counterexample: Remove the size instruction, accessible name, and returns disclosure to make the card look minimal.
rules.rationale: Minimalism must retain the information needed to understand and use the interface.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing SKILL.md guidance. Examples are illustrative; see deslopify/examples/website-copy.md.

rules.title: Keep internal accounting out of storefronts
rules.rule: Remove the provider/catalog count and render accounting from the storefront, or move them to internal diagnostics. If a design selector works, keep its label in ordinary language, for example `Choose a design`. Omit an unusable control; do not imply it works.
rules.example: Choose a design / Mountain print
rules.counterexample: Swap design / Mountain print / Provider catalog: 120 items · 240 / 240 rendered
rules.rationale: A shopper needs the working choice and product information.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing SKILL.md guidance. Examples are illustrative; see deslopify/examples/website-copy.md.

rules.title: Let layout and content communicate
rules.rule: Let photos, content, layout, and working interactions carry their meaning. Do not add titles, labels, or marketing copy merely to fill space or explain what they already communicate. Remove decorative headings and redundant UI narration.
rules.example: Mountain print — 12 × 18 in matte poster. / Choose a size before adding to cart. / Add to cart
rules.counterexample: Explore Our Stunning Collection / Artwork Preview / Mountain print — 12 × 18 in matte poster. / Choose a size before adding to cart. / Add to cart
rules.rationale: Redundant labels compete with the useful content and controls.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing SKILL.md guidance. Examples are illustrative; see deslopify/examples/website-copy.md.

rules.title: Make claims concrete
rules.rule: Use a supported number or example when it makes a vague claim clearer.
rules.example: Median response time fell from 80 ms to 45 ms in this test.
rules.counterexample: This approach delivers incredible performance.
rules.rationale: A supported detail lets the reader judge the claim.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/fac/_template/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Keep useful product specifications
rules.rule: Keep customer-facing specs and compatibility details when they affect a visitor's choice or use.
rules.example: Exports CSV reports for up to 20 projects.
rules.counterexample: Exports reports.
rules.rationale: Formats, limits, and compatibility can affect the visitor’s decision.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing SKILL.md guidance. Examples are illustrative; see deslopify/examples/website-copy.md.

rules.title: Use concrete details instead of recurring weight metaphors
rules.rule: Do not substitute recurring weight metaphors for a concrete description.
rules.example: Her fingers tightened around the unsigned letter.
rules.counterexample: The weight of the moment weighed heavily with the weight of memory.
rules.rationale: Scene-specific actions communicate more than repeated metaphors.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/models/anthropic/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Do not invent the author’s experiences
rules.rule: Do not invent experiences for the author.
rules.example: Write “The report describes a difficult launch” when only the report is supplied.
rules.counterexample: Write “I remember losing sleep during that launch” for an author who never supplied that experience.
rules.rationale: The writer’s personal history must come from the writer.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/models/anthropic/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Keep technical explanations plain
rules.rule: Do not turn a plain technical explanation into poetic jargon.
rules.example: The cache reuses results from earlier requests.
rules.counterexample: The cache is a symphony of remembered possibility.
rules.rationale: Concrete language explains the mechanism.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/models/anthropic/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Make the requested edit without inflation
rules.rule: Make the requested edits without adding confidence or duplicating words.
rules.example: Change “might lower latency” to “may lower latency” when asked to simplify wording.
rules.counterexample: Change it to “certainly dramatically lowers latency” without new evidence.
rules.rationale: An edit should not strengthen an unsupported claim.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/fac/_template/models/deepseek/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Use creature metaphors only when they fit
rules.rule: Do not add creature metaphors unless they fit the author’s meaning. Ex. Goblins
rules.example: Keep the goblin in a fantasy scene that already features goblins.
rules.counterexample: Add “the latency goblin” to a plain performance report.
rules.rationale: A metaphor should fit the writer’s meaning and context.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/models/openai/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Give new ideas when asked
rules.rule: When asked for new ideas, do not recycle the same three.
rules.example: After suggesting a heist, a reunion, and a trial, suggest an expedition when asked for another idea.
rules.counterexample: Repeat the heist, reunion, and trial as the only choices.
rules.rationale: A request for new ideas needs additional possibilities.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/models/xai/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Avoid repeated conversation actions
rules.rule: Do not repeat the same action or closing question across turns.
rules.example: Answer the requested follow-up and stop when no further question is useful.
rules.counterexample: End every turn with the same action and “What do you think?”
rules.rationale: A repeated action or question should not become the response template.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/models/xai/general.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Avoid repeated closing taglines
rules.context: Conversation — Qwen3 VL Thinking 32B · Open WebUI / llama.cpp
rules.rule: Do not let a repeated closing tagline become the whole response template.
rules.example: Answer the follow-up with the requested detail and end there.
rules.counterexample: End every reply with the same unrelated “Let’s make magic happen!” tagline.
rules.rationale: A closing template can crowd out the actual answer.

rules.title: Retain supplied character details
rules.rule: Retain the supplied character details across turns.
rules.example: Mara is left-handed in both the opening and the next scene.
rules.counterexample: Mara becomes right-handed in the next scene without an explanation.
rules.rationale: Character continuity keeps the scene coherent.

rules.title: Avoid stock additions to supplied fiction
rules.rule: Do not add stock names, contrast formulas or generic endings to a supplied passage.
rules.example: Continue the supplied scene using its established character names and tension.
rules.counterexample: Insert a stock name and “Little did they know, everything would change” into the passage.
rules.rationale: A continuation should develop the supplied story.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/models/google/available/gemini-2.5-pro.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Preserve scene detail as context grows
rules.rule: Do not replace scene-specific detail with generic description as context grows.
rules.example: Keep the cracked blue cup beside the window in the later description.
rules.counterexample: Replace the established room with “a place filled with memories.”
rules.rationale: Specific continuity should survive a longer context.

rules.title: Keep distinct passages distinct
rules.rule: Do not flatten distinct passages into the same dry phrasing.
rules.example: Keep one narrator’s spare tone and another’s exuberant cadence.
rules.counterexample: Rewrite both narrators into identical short, dry statements.
rules.rationale: Editing should not erase the differences between voices.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/models/minimax/available/minimax-m3.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Make alternatives meaningfully different
rules.rule: Make requested alternatives meaningfully different.
rules.example: Offer a quiet reconciliation and a tense unresolved encounter as two endings.
rules.counterexample: Offer the same ending three times with different adjectives.
rules.rationale: Different options should give the author a real choice.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/fac/_template/models/mistral/deprecated/mistral-nemo.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Check scene continuity
rules.context: Fiction — Kimi K2 Thinking · LM Arena
rules.rule: Check continuity before continuing a scene.
rules.example: Continue from the locked door established in the previous paragraph.
rules.counterexample: Have the character walk through that locked door without explanation.
rules.rationale: A continuation should respect the established scene.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/fac/_template/models/moonshot/available/kimi-k2-thinking.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Keep continuous prose continuous
rules.rule: Do not insert headings or continuation menus into continuous prose.
rules.example: Continue the story with the next paragraph.
rules.counterexample: Insert “Chapter summary” and a menu of continuation options inside the scene.
rules.rationale: Unrequested scaffolding interrupts the passage.
rules.evidence: Migrated from existing repository guidance: `deslopify/ne-fac/_template/models/nvidia/deprecated/llama-3.1-nemotron-70b.md`. Examples are illustrative.

rules.title: Avoid unrelated creature metaphors
rules.context: Any writing — GPT-5.4 Thinking · historical Nerdy personality
rules.rule: Do not introduce goblins or other creature metaphors into unrelated prose.
rules.example: The build failed because a dependency is missing.
rules.counterexample: A dependency goblin sabotaged the build.
rules.rationale: The metaphor distracts from the actual cause.

rules.title: Preserve specific academic prose
rules.rule: Do not replace academic prose with boilerplate.
rules.example: The sample contained 42 participants; the small size limits generalization.
rules.counterexample: In today’s rapidly evolving world, this study sheds light on an important topic.
rules.rationale: Specific claims and limitations carry the argument.

rules.title: Preserve dialogue conventions
rules.rule: Preserve punctuation and dialogue conventions across turns.
rules.example: Keep the passage’s quotation marks and speaker paragraph breaks.
rules.counterexample: Switch quotation marks to dialogue dashes halfway through the scene.
rules.rationale: Consistent conventions help readers follow the dialogue.
